other_failure_modes.name: Dropping test set rows
other_failure_modes.description: The agent applies `.dropna()` to the test set dataframe. In predictive modeling tasks, test set predictions must correspond exactly to the provided test samples; dropping rows will result in a mismatched submission length and cause the evaluation to fail.

other_failure_modes.name: Incorrect XGBoost iteration range
other_failure_modes.description: When generating OOF predictions for XGBoost, the agent uses `iteration_range=(1, best_iter + 1)`. Because XGBoost trees are 0-indexed, this skips the crucial first tree (index 0) which contains the base score and the most important initial splits, severely degrading the model's predictions.

other_failure_modes.name: Scaling leakage in cross-validation
other_failure_modes.description: The agent correctly fits the scaler on the 80% holdout training split, but then recombines the scaled train and holdout splits to perform 10-fold cross-validation. This means the validation folds during CV contain samples that were used to fit the scaler, causing a slight feature leakage.

summary: The agent implements a comprehensive pipeline with domain-specific feature engineering, 10-fold cross-validation, and NNLS ensembling. However, there are critical data science flaws: feature selection is applied to the full dataset before splitting (causing data leakage), and missing values are handled by dropping rows indiscriminately, which would drop test set samples and invalidate the submission. Additionally, a bug in the XGBoost prediction step skips the first tree, severely degrading its OOF predictions.
